anzsic_codes.name: Other Electrical and Electronic Goods Wholesaling

merger_description:
Schneider Electric Industries SAS (**Schneider Electric**), through its wholly owned subsidiary SE 2026 A, proposes to acquire sole control of Shelly Group SE (**Shelly**) by way of certain individual over-the-counter share acquisitions and through the completion of a voluntary public takeover offer (the **Acquisition**).

Schneider Electric is headquartered in France and listed on Euronext Paris. Schneider Electric is an international group that is mainly active in power management (medium voltage, low voltage and secure power), and in various types of software solutions and products for automation and energy management of commercial, industrial and infrastructure customers. It also provides smart home automation solutions as an ancillary offering of its business, including in Australia.

Shelly is a Bulgaria-headquartered technology company dual listed on the Bulgarian Stock Exchange and the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in Germany. Shelly is active in the development, production and sale of smart home automation solutions under the Shelly brand. Shelly primarily focuses on the supply of smart home automation solutions in Europe but also supplies smart home automation products into Australia. Shelly does not have any offices or employees in Australia.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between Schneider
Electric (and its connected entities) and Shelly in the supply
of smart home automation products in Australia
b. the parties’ combined share of the supply of smart home
automation products in Australia is estimated to be low and
the increment arising from the Acquisition is expected to be
small
c. there are alternative providers of smart home automation
products to customers in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
